review_notes: I read the whole file and the simp lemmas in Presburger/Basic.lean (funMap_zero/one/add, realize_*). I also read withConstants_funMap_sumInl and withConstants_funMap_sumInr in ModelTheory/LanguageMap.lean. I did not run Lean. I did not check why the @[simp] lemma fails to fire, so the proposed fix (a Presburger-specific simp lemma, or fixing the unifier-facing statement) is a suggestion that I haven't tested. I found no loops or competing rules in this file. The long `simp only` list at lines 46–50 is unconventional but acceptable.

findings.problem: `withConstants_funMap_sumInl` is tagged `@[simp]`, but in this file it has to be applied by a manual `rw` three times, at the zero, one and add cases. The same lemma carries a Semantics.lean comment saying it "does not work with simp for some reason". So the simp set for `funMap` on `Sum.inl` symbols in `presburger[[A]]` is unreliable: the `funMap_zero`, `funMap_one` and `funMap_add` lemmas in Presburger/Basic.lean fire only after a manual rewrite. The `add` case also needs a hand-written chain of `add_left_comm`/`add_assoc`.
findings.proposed_change: Add presburger-specific simp lemmas in Presburger/Basic.lean. They should state `funMap` (or `Term.realize` of `func (Sum.inl f) ts`) for `presburger[[A]]` directly, in a form whose instance arguments unify under simp. Alternatively, fix the unification problem in `withConstants_funMap_sumInl` itself. Then the `rw [withConstants_funMap_sumInl]` lines can become plain `simp [ih]`.
findings.benefit: Proofs about terms over `presburger[[A]]` can use simp directly, without remembering the manual rewrite. The `@[simp]` attribute on the generic lemma would then match what simp actually does.
